title: Per-backend filter recommendation, configuration, tests and docs
description: From the study results decide keep/adjust/remove per backend, implement per-backend defaults with an on/off/auto override (API, CLI flag, config key), update tests and docs, and report the numbers table.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Recommendation implemented: keep the coding-domain filter for VADER only, per-backend configurable. The filter stays essential for VADER (tuning 1.000 with vs 0.735 without; combined 0.767 vs 0.600; probes 17/19 vs 9/19 technical-use neu) and is redundant-and-harmful for the go_emotions transformer (gold accuracies identical with/without at 0.971/0.731/0.867; filter flips one genuine-frustration probe neg->neu and another neg->pos) so every transformer spec now carries defaultCodingFilter=false and VADER defaults true; 'auto' (the default) resolves per backend, 'on'/'off' override. Wiring: --sentiment-coding-filter on|off|auto CLI flag (invalid values rejected) and sentimentCodingFilter config key, threaded through run.ts to createSentimentBackendAsync. Tests: codingFilterFor resolution matrix, vader raw-vs-filter probe behavior, registry defaultCodingFilter=false assertions for all four transformer specs, CLI default-filter/on-off JSON counts and invalid-value rejection. Docs: README coding-domain-overrides bullet and wiki epic-M section with the full six-config table. Full suite: 197 suites, 1617 passed, 2 skipped; build clean; lint unchanged (one pre-existing error in benchmark packet-validation spec).
